text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty INC-5612 triggered — high TLS handshake failures + ALB target health flapping in us-west-2. Alert: 5xx_rate=18.4% (5m), unhealthy_targets=42%

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-5612 created and notified on-call (sara). Escalation policy: network-lb -> oncall-ops.

sara: Acked. I'm the on-call for this window, starting triage. TL;DR: customers seeing 502/524, spikes started ~10:02 PDT. Going to check recent infra changes.

josh: I'm pulling ALB metrics now. I see a spike in TLS handshake errors and TargetHealth unhealthy_count increased right after a listener update at 09:58. That matches.

deepa: grabbing health check logs from target group tg-0a1b2c3d:

```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:111222333:targetgroup/tg-0a1b2c3d
{
  "TargetHealthDescriptions": [
    {"Target": {"Id": "i-0aa0bb0cc"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "Health check failed"}},
    {"Target": {"Id": "i-0dd0ee0ff"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "TLS handshake failure"}}
  ]
}
```

carlos: looking at ALB listener change in deploy logs — we rolled a TLS policy update (enable TLS1.3-only cipher policy) in canary at 09:56, then promoted at 09:59. Some clients/old kernels and our health check agent don't support TLS1.3-only ciphers. That would explain handshake failures + targets marked unhealthy.

sara: that makes sense. deepa, can you run an openssl check from the health-check subnet?

deepa: running:

```
openssl s_client -connect internal-target-01:443 -servername internal-target
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735...: TLS handshake failure: no shared cipher
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

josh: yep. health check client can't negotiate. Also saw a couple of DNS anomalies — some EDNS caches still return old IPs for api.redwood.ai in a subset of edge PoPs from last config change yesterday. Running a quick dig:

```
# from prod-dns-cache-1
dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
52.34.210.11
52.34.210.12

# from stale-cache-1
dig +short api.redwood.ai @stale-cache-1
52.34.210.11  # only primary, missing new LB IPs
```

sara: combination is bad — TLS policy broke health checks, and partial DNS propagation left some clients hitting the new listener only. Next steps: revert TLS policy change on ALB listener to the previous policy (TLS1.2+), reweight traffic away from canary TG, force-target-recovery. I'll perform rollback now.

josh: I'll prepare a quick traffic reweight to the stable target group and increase health check grace if needed. If rollback reduces handshake failures, we can then evaluate a staged reapply with a dual-policy listener.

sara: executing rollback:

```
# rollback ALB listener TLS policy to ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:111222333:listener/app/redwood-alb/50dc6c495c0c9188/abcd1234 --ssl-policy ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017
# reweight canary -> stable
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn ... --default-actions '[{"Type":"forward","ForwardConfig":{"TargetGroups":[{"TargetGroupArn":"arn:...:tg-stable","Weight":100},{"TargetGroupArn":"arn:...:tg-canary","Weight":0}]}}]'
```

pagerduty-bot: INC-5612 acknowledged by sara. Priority: P1. Notifying escalation path.

oncall-ops: Noted. I'm watching network egress and DNS cache invalidation jobs. Will bump DNS TTLs where safe and flush caches in affected PoPs.

deepa: after rollback, quick check from health-check subnet shows:

```
openssl s_client -connect internal-target-01:443 -servername internal-target
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
certificate chain
subject=CN=internal-target
---
SSL handshake has read 4121 bytes and written 456 bytes
---
```

carlos: ALB target health now returning healthy for previously failing instances. Metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 2.3% within 4 minutes after rollback and reweight. Some DNS caches still show old IPs; oncall-ops is purging caches in 3 PoPs.

sara: customer impact summary for postmortem: impacted region us-west-2 (primary), partial effect in eu-west due to DNS caches. Affected customers include AcmeCorp and BetaHealth (they reported increased 502s). Rough magnitude: ~120 errors/min at peak, ~2.1% of total requests for 12 minutes. No data loss reported.

josh: initiating a controlled test to reapply a safer TLS policy (enable TLS1.3 but keep TLS1.2 fallback) and will do canary at 1% for 15m. I'll open a follow-up thread for the TLS rollout plan.

sara: handing off monitoring to josh — I have a calendar meeting starting now. I'll remain reachable if anything regresses.

josh: taking over. I'll watch for 30m and coordinate the TLS reapply plan with deepa and oncall-ops. Will update incident once stable.

pagerduty-bot: INC-5612 updated: status=mitigated, assignee=josh. Please keep updates in this thread.

sara: thanks team — add to postmortem: root cause = premature TLS policy promotion + insufficient health-check compatibility testing + partial DNS propagation interactions. Action items: stricter rollout gating for ALB TLS changes, add health-check client TLS matrix to CI, lower risk DNS TTL change windows.

josh: confirmed metrics stable at 0.6% 5xx for 20m. I'll close the incident after 1h of stability and post a follow-up with exact numbers and timeline.

incident-bot: Note: please run the incident template in #postmortems and add the timeline + runbook link: https://redwood.atlassian/incident/inc-5612
